en.value: Find out the number of equivalence classes that can be defined by the set {4, 5, 6}:

english.explanation: (1) Reflexive relation – A relation R on set A is said to be reflexive if (a, a) is there in relation R ∀a ∈A. (2) Symmetric relation – A relation R on set is said to be symmetric if (a, b) is there in relation R then (b, a) should also be there in relation R ∀ a, b ∈ A. (3) Transitive relation – A relation R on set A is said to be transitive if (a, b) and (b, c) are there in the relation R then (a, c) should also be there in the relation R ∀ a, b, c ∈A. A relation is an equivalence relation if it is reflexive, symmetric and transitive. Now, equivalence relations that can be defined on the set {4, 5, 6} are- (1) {(4, 4), (5, 5), (6, 6)} (2) {(4, 4), (5, 5), (6, 6), (4, 5), (5, 4)} (3) {(4, 4), (5, 5), (6, 6), (4, 6), (6, 4)} (4) {(4, 4), (5, 5), (6, 6), (5, 6), (6, 5)} (5) {(4, 4), (5, 5), (6, 6), (4, 5), (5, 4), (4, 6), (6, 4), (5, 6), (6, 5)} Thus number of equivalence relation is 5.

en.value: Calculate the number of asymptotes for the function f (x) = (x ÷ (x2 – 9)).

english.explanation: An asymptotes are lines that a curve approaches as it moves towards infinity. Distance between the curve and an asymptote tends to be zero as one move towards infinity. There are three types of asymptotes– 1) Vertical Asymptotes 2) Horizontal Asymptotes 3) Oblique Asymptotes Now for a rational function with n and m being the degrees of numerator and denominator respectively we have 1) if n < m, then, the x-axis (y = 0) is the horizontal asymptote. 2) if n = m then, horizontal asymptote is the line y = a b 3) if n > m there is no horizontal asymptote (There is an oblique asymptotes) Now f(x) 2 x x 9 = − clearly has y = 0 as the horizontal asymptote and since f (x) is undefined at x = +3, –3 we get that there are two vertical asymptotes namely x = +3, and x = –3. Thus, total no. of asymptotes is 3.
